subject.title: [Bug] PTY silently disabled in sandbox mode without warning when pty:true is set

question: For explicit `pty: true` in sandboxed exec, should OpenClaw warn and continue without PTY, or fail the tool call instead?
rationale: The issue touches sandboxed execution semantics, and the report explicitly allows either an informational warning or a stricter failure; automation should not choose that security-boundary behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Warn And Continue
options.body: Emit a clear warning when sandbox mode disables explicit PTY while preserving current sandboxed non-PTY execution behavior.

options.title: Fail Explicit PTY
options.body: Reject sandboxed exec calls that explicitly request PTY so users must choose a different host, elevated path, or non-PTY command.

options.title: Adopt Or Replace The Fork PR
options.body: After the behavior choice, review the open fork candidate or open a narrow replacement in `openclaw/openclaw` with tests and docs.

recommendation.title: Warn And Continue
recommendation.body: Emit a clear warning when sandbox mode disables explicit PTY while preserving current sandboxed non-PTY execution behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest history signal for the original PTY behavior, fallback behavior, and adjacent exec docs/runtime decisions.
